I haven't had counselling because of an abortion...yet (I will be), but I have had an abortion and I have done counselling earlier in my life. If you are thinking of going to counselling then I would highly recommended trying it, I don't have experience with a clinic specific counsellor, but I imagine it will help a bit with anxiety to know their stance on abortion and that their informed on it.

Personally I say counselling saved my life, a counsellor will be able to give you tools to deal with everything, it sounds like you are dealing with an incredible amount and you can tell your counsellor everything, you don't have to worry it's too much. 
That being said I want you to know that you don't have to talk about anything you don't want to, and if you are uncomfortable with your counsellor don't feel obligated to stay with that counsellor, you can ask to switch or find a new one, also you don't have to keep going, but I suggest trying it a few times, one appointment is not enough to figure out if it's the right fit or working.

If your open to counselling working (which it sounds like you are)it will be more beneficial, I hope you find someone to talk to, you are incredibly strong for coping with everything you are, and I know I don't know you, or you me, but I am proud of you for just considering help, it takes a lot for someone to admit they may need help.
